reviewer: ChatGPT author self-review; not an independent human or corpus audit

entries.languageReview: Consideration invites evaluation; reference supplies background information.
entries.pragmaticReview: for your consideration: It does not specify whether a decision is required; add a deadline and explicit request when necessary.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Information provides awareness; an instruction tells the reader what to do.
entries.pragmaticReview: for your information: Spoken with heavy stress, this phrase can sound defensive or corrective; FYI is briefer and less formal.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: For the record establishes a fact explicitly; off the record asks that remarks not be publicly attributed.
entries.pragmaticReview: for the record: It may signal disagreement with an existing account; keep the following statement factual rather than accusatory.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Discussed confirms a conversation took place; agreed confirms a shared decision.
entries.pragmaticReview: as discussed: Do not use a prior discussion as evidence that someone accepted your proposal.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Agreed implies acceptance; proposed only indicates a suggestion.
entries.pragmaticReview: as agreed: Use this only when agreement actually exists; otherwise it can pressure the reader through a false assumption.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Requested refers to what someone asked for; agreed refers to a mutual decision.
entries.pragmaticReview: as requested: Identify the document or change clearly so the reader can see how the request was fulfilled.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Outlined means main points were presented; specified suggests precise details were given.
entries.pragmaticReview: as outlined: An outline is not necessarily a full specification, so do not imply every detail was settled.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: With regard to introduces a subject; because of introduces a cause.
entries.pragmaticReview: with regard to: With regards to is widespread, but with regard to is the conventional edited form; regarding is more concise.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: In response to identifies the trigger for a reaction; in relation to only establishes a connection.
entries.pragmaticReview: in response to: It can describe actions as well as written replies; specify which feedback led to which change.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: In relation to marks a connection; in response to marks a reaction.
entries.pragmaticReview: in relation to: About is often clearer in everyday email; the longer phrase suits formal correspondence.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: On behalf of means representing someone; for may simply mean benefiting them.
entries.pragmaticReview: on behalf of: Representation implies authority or permission; do not imply you speak for everyone without that basis.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: In accordance with indicates compliance; in line with may indicate broad consistency.
entries.pragmaticReview: in accordance with: Common in official rules; use following or under when those give the same meaning more simply.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: In line with indicates consistency; identical to requires exact sameness.
entries.pragmaticReview: in line with: Two values may be broadly in line without matching exactly; give numbers when the tolerance matters.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Subject to makes an offer conditional; confirmed states that the condition has been satisfied.
entries.pragmaticReview: subject to: Keep the condition visible rather than burying it after an apparently unconditional promise.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: With immediate effect starts now; from Monday starts at a specified future point.
entries.pragmaticReview: with immediate effect: Official notices should include the date or time if readers may receive them later.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Until further notice is indefinite but changeable; permanently rules out planned resumption.
entries.pragmaticReview: until further notice: Give an update channel because the phrase itself supplies no end date.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: This phrase leaves timing flexible; by Friday gives an explicit deadline.
entries.pragmaticReview: at your earliest convenience: It can sound pressuring despite its polite form; use a specific date when timing is important.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Close of business refers to the working day's end; midnight ends the calendar day.
entries.pragmaticReview: by close of business: COB is ambiguous across teams and time zones; specify the clock time and zone for important deadlines.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Attached means included as a file; below means in the body of the message.
entries.pragmaticReview: please find attached: The phrase is correct but traditional; I have attached is often warmer and more direct.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Please note that highlights information; please confirm that requests verification.
entries.pragmaticReview: please note that: It draws attention but does not prove the recipient has read or accepted the information.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: This construction requests an action politely; I appreciate it thanks someone for help already given.
entries.pragmaticReview: I would appreciate it if: Would and could soften the request, but a demanding tone can still make it sound like an order.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Confirm verifies a detail; explain gives reasons or describes how something works.
entries.pragmaticReview: could you confirm: Use whether when uncertain; confirm that can imply you already expect the statement to be true.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Advise is the verb; advice is the uncountable noun.
entries.pragmaticReview: please advise: It is concise but can sound abrupt; Could you advise how to proceed? is gentler.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Enquire asks for information; request asks for information or an action directly.
entries.pragmaticReview: I am writing to enquire: Enquire is common in British correspondence; inquire is also correct, especially in American English.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Acknowledging a report is not the same as accepting that every allegation is proven.
entries.pragmaticReview: thank you for bringing this to my attention: Follow the thanks with an appropriate check or action so it does not feel like an empty response.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Patience is willingness to wait; patients are people receiving medical care.
entries.pragmaticReview: thank you for your patience: It acknowledges waiting but does not replace an apology or a realistic update when you caused a delay.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Inconvenience describes trouble or disruption; serious harm deserves a more specific acknowledgement.
entries.pragmaticReview: sorry for the inconvenience: For a major loss this phrase can minimise impact; name the actual problem and explain the remedy.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: This is a formal apology; excuse me usually addresses a minor immediate interruption.
entries.pragmaticReview: please accept my apologies: An apology is stronger when it names responsibility and repair rather than asking the recipient to dismiss the problem.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: To is a preposition here, so it takes hearing; hope to hear uses an infinitive.
entries.pragmaticReview: I look forward to hearing from you: The closing welcomes a reply but sets no deadline; state timing separately when required.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Acknowledging receipt confirms arrival; approving confirms acceptance of the contents.
entries.pragmaticReview: acknowledge receipt: Receipt alone does not create agreement, so avoid treating a delivery acknowledgement as consent.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Seek clarification removes ambiguity; seek approval asks for permission.
entries.pragmaticReview: seek clarification: Seek takes a direct object without for; ask for clarification is the alternative construction.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Requesting an extension asks for more time; announcing a delay does not ask permission.
entries.pragmaticReview: request an extension: Give the proposed date and reason; the request does not change the deadline until accepted.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: An update reports changes since the previous information; an overview explains the whole situation.
entries.pragmaticReview: provide an update: State what changed, what remains unresolved and the next expected event.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Raise a concern flags a possible problem; make an accusation asserts wrongdoing.
entries.pragmaticReview: raise a concern: Describe evidence and likely impact without assuming motives; a concern can be valid before its cause is known.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Escalation seeks higher authority; complaining simply expresses dissatisfaction.
entries.pragmaticReview: escalate an issue: Explain the decision or help needed so escalation does not sound like a threat.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: A revised timeline changes timing; a revised scope changes what work is included.
entries.pragmaticReview: revised timeline: Show changed milestones and dependencies rather than merely replacing the final date.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Proposed marks a suggestion; agreed marks an accepted approach.
entries.pragmaticReview: proposed approach: Keep recommendation and approval status separate so readers know whether to comment or begin.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: An outcome is the intended result; an output is a produced item that may help achieve it.
entries.pragmaticReview: agreed outcome: Agreement on a broad outcome does not imply agreement on every method or measure.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Next steps identify actions; aspirations describe desired results without a route.
entries.pragmaticReview: next steps: Assign owners and dates to prevent a list of intentions from being mistaken for a plan.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Outstanding here means unresolved, not exceptionally good.
entries.pragmaticReview: outstanding action: Name the owner and due date; outstanding does not by itself mean overdue.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: A decision log tracks choices and reasons; meeting minutes cover a wider record of a meeting.
entries.pragmaticReview: decision log: Useful entries include date, owner, alternatives and rationale so later readers understand the choice.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Minutes are a concise meeting record; a transcript reproduces speech much more fully.
entries.pragmaticReview: meeting minutes: Record decisions and actions accurately without implying that every spoken comment was approved.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: A point of contact handles communication; a decision-maker has authority to approve.
entries.pragmaticReview: point of contact: The contact may coordinate answers without owning every decision; state escalation routes where needed.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Handover notes support transfer of responsibility; personal notes may lack the context a successor needs.
entries.pragmaticReview: handover notes: Include open issues and next actions, not just a history of completed work.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Sign-off is approval; acknowledgement only confirms something was received or noticed.
entries.pragmaticReview: sign-off: The noun is hyphenated; the verb is sign off, as in sign off the design.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Approval in principle supports the broad idea; final approval authorises proceeding under settled conditions.
entries.pragmaticReview: approval in principle: List remaining conditions explicitly because people may otherwise mistake preliminary support for permission.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Written confirmation records an arrangement; a verbal assurance is spoken and may be harder to check later.
entries.pragmaticReview: written confirmation: It should state the relevant terms; a vague email saying fine may leave important details uncertain.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Documentation is uncountable; documents are individual countable items.
entries.pragmaticReview: supporting documentation: Name the required evidence and acceptable format instead of asking for unnecessary personal records.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Clarification required asks for precision; rejected records a negative decision.
entries.pragmaticReview: clarification required: A helpful status names the ambiguous field and the exact question to answer.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Given that takes a clause; given takes a noun phrase such as given the rain.
entries.pragmaticReview: given that: It presents the reason as accepted information; do not use it to disguise a disputed assumption.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Provided that sets a condition; given that states an accepted reason.
entries.pragmaticReview: provided that: Future conditions normally use present tense here; the phrase is more formal than as long as.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: In this sense as long as means provided that; it does not measure duration.
entries.pragmaticReview: as long as: A condition may remain active throughout an activity, as in keeping noise low.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Assuming that uses an unverified premise; given that usually treats the premise as established.
entries.pragmaticReview: assuming that: State important assumptions openly so a forecast can be revised if they fail.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: On condition that makes a requirement explicit; unless states the exception preventing an outcome.
entries.pragmaticReview: on condition that: Often stronger and more contractual than as long as; make the required action unambiguous.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: In the event of takes a noun phrase; in the event that takes a clause.
entries.pragmaticReview: in the event of: Common in contingency notices; ordinary if is often clearer in conversation.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: In case motivates a precaution now; if makes the action conditional on an event.
entries.pragmaticReview: in case: The precaution happens before the possible problem, which is why in case and if are not interchangeable.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Even if considers a possibility; even though acknowledges a real fact.
entries.pragmaticReview: even if: It stresses that the condition will not change the decision, even if that condition seems difficult.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Whether introduces alternatives; weather refers to atmospheric conditions.
entries.pragmaticReview: whether or not: In reply whether or not you can attend, both yes and no responses are requested.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Despite takes a noun or -ing form; although introduces a clause.
entries.pragmaticReview: despite: Do not add of after despite; use in spite of when that three-word form is intended.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: In spite of and despite share this meaning; despite is shorter.
entries.pragmaticReview: in spite of: Write spite as a separate word; spiteful emotion is not the meaning of this fixed expression.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Although subordinates a contrasting clause; but coordinates two clauses.
entries.pragmaticReview: although: Do not normally pair although and but for the same contrast in standard written English.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Even though emphasises a real contrast; even if covers a hypothetical condition.
entries.pragmaticReview: even though: It adds emphasis compared with although, especially when the outcome is surprising.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Whereas contrasts facts; because gives a reason.
entries.pragmaticReview: whereas: Use parallel information on both sides so readers can compare the same dimension or alternatives.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: While here means although; it does not indicate simultaneous time.
entries.pragmaticReview: while: Use although if readers might interpret while as a time relationship.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: However is a linking adverb; but is a coordinating conjunction.
entries.pragmaticReview: however: In edited writing, do not join two complete clauses with only a comma before however.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Nonetheless means despite that; moreover adds support without contrast.
entries.pragmaticReview: nonetheless: It often signals a surprising result that survives the previous limitation; it is more written than conversational.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Sentence-initial still can mean nevertheless; mid-clause still often means continuing.
entries.pragmaticReview: still: Pause after initial still to signal the contrast rather than ongoing time.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Yet as a conjunction contrasts facts; not yet describes an action still pending.
entries.pragmaticReview: yet: It often highlights a surprising combination and can also link adjectives.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Even so refers back to a stated situation; even if introduces a possible condition.
entries.pragmaticReview: even so: It concedes the previous point without allowing it to settle the conclusion.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: That said qualifies your previous statement; therefore draws a consequence.
entries.pragmaticReview: that said: Often conversational in tone; the second point should genuinely balance the first.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Having said that qualifies your earlier point; as mentioned repeats or refers to it.
entries.pragmaticReview: having said that: It is a discourse formula rather than a literal report of when you spoke; avoid using it for unrelated topic changes.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: On the other hand offers another side; on the contrary rejects the previous claim.
entries.pragmaticReview: on the other hand: On the one hand is optional when the first side is already clear.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: By contrast emphasises difference; similarly emphasises likeness.
entries.pragmaticReview: by contrast: Use comparable subjects so the contrast is meaningful rather than a switch to unrelated information.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Conversely reverses a relationship; however introduces a broader contrast.
entries.pragmaticReview: conversely: A reverse claim is not automatically logically true; check its evidence rather than assuming symmetry.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Rather than contrasts alternatives; instead of explicitly substitutes one for another.
entries.pragmaticReview: rather than: Keep parallel grammar after shared auxiliaries: should clarify rather than add.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Instead of takes a noun or -ing form; instead alone can link a separate sentence.
entries.pragmaticReview: instead of: The phrase specifies the replaced alternative, so make both options clear.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Regardless of removes a factor from the decision; despite acknowledges an obstacle.
entries.pragmaticReview: regardless of: It does not mean all factors are irrelevant, only the one named after of.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Irrespective of and regardless of overlap; irrespective of is generally more formal.
entries.pragmaticReview: irrespective of: Avoid needless formality in a casual invitation; whatever your department may be clearer.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Except for removes an exception; including adds something to the group.
entries.pragmaticReview: except for: It often qualifies a general judgement rather than listing every excluded item.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Apart from can mean except for; it can also mean in addition to in other contexts.
entries.pragmaticReview: apart from: Here it excludes an exception; make the sentence clear enough to avoid the additive interpretation.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Than marks comparison or exception; then marks time or sequence.
entries.pragmaticReview: other than: Especially natural after negatives such as no, nothing and nobody.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Save for means except for here; it does not mean preserve something for later.
entries.pragmaticReview: save for: This is literary or formal; except for is usually more natural in ordinary conversation.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Insofar as limits degree or scope; because presents a cause.
entries.pragmaticReview: insofar as: It is formal and can sound legalistic; to the extent that is often easier to process.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: To the extent that marks degree; provided that usually establishes a yes-or-no condition.
entries.pragmaticReview: to the extent that: The claim may hold partly rather than completely; identify which aspect limits it.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: In terms of selects a comparison dimension; overall combines multiple considerations.
entries.pragmaticReview: in terms of: Name a useful dimension; the phrase adds little if it only repeats the subject.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: As far as I know limits certainty; I can confirm asserts verification.
entries.pragmaticReview: as far as: It signals an information boundary and should not substitute for checking a crucial fact.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: As for shifts attention to a topic; as far as usually introduces a limit or perspective.
entries.pragmaticReview: as for: With a sharp tone it can imply irritation, especially before naming a person.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: To is a preposition here; it takes a noun or -ing form.
entries.pragmaticReview: when it comes to: It foregrounds a subject conversationally; regarding may fit a very concise formal note.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: This refers to prior information; bear in mind asks someone to remember a point.
entries.pragmaticReview: with this in mind: Make the reference clear; several preceding facts can make this ambiguous.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: For this reason points back to a cause; for example introduces an illustration.
entries.pragmaticReview: for this reason: The preceding fact must actually support the conclusion; proximity alone does not establish causation.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Owing to takes a noun phrase; because takes a clause.
entries.pragmaticReview: owing to: It sounds more formal than because of and is common in notices.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Due to takes a noun phrase; because introduces a full clause.
entries.pragmaticReview: due to: Sentence-initial due to is standard in much modern usage; older restrictions are not universal rules.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: In consequence links a result; in consequence of introduces its cause.
entries.pragmaticReview: in consequence: The phrase is formal and less conversational than as a result; do not use it merely to mean afterwards.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Therefore marks an inference or result; however marks contrast.
entries.pragmaticReview: therefore: A valid grammatical connection does not prove the reasoning; check that the conclusion follows.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Accordingly means in a fitting way; according to introduces the source or standard explicitly.
entries.pragmaticReview: accordingly: The required adjustment is inferred from earlier information; specify it if readers could interpret it differently.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: In this sense as such means in that capacity; therefore means for that reason.
entries.pragmaticReview: as such: Make the preceding role or category explicit so such has a clear referent.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: In turn here links a further consequence; taking turns alternates participants.
entries.pragmaticReview: in turn: Keep the causal chain credible; it does not mean every later event was caused by the earlier one.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Moreover adds support; nevertheless introduces a concession.
entries.pragmaticReview: moreover: It is relatively formal and can sound heavy in casual conversation; also often suffices.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Furthermore adds another supporting point; for instance supplies an example of a point.
entries.pragmaticReview: furthermore: Use it to develop an argument, not simply to decorate a list of unrelated facts.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.

entries.languageReview: Besides adds a reason; beside means next to.
entries.pragmaticReview: besides: In conversation it can present a reason as decisive and sometimes sound dismissive of further debate.
entries.evidenceLimit: Editorial usefulness and level estimate; no independent corpus-frequency claim.
